My AI policy

If a project doesn't have an AI_POLICY.md, this is my personal policy:

  • All AI assisted commits will have an Assisted-by: <Harness>:<model> trailer.
  • All AI generated text in descriptions, comments, etc. will be marked by 🤖 _AI text below_ 🤖 or otherwise clearly indicated (detail block, etc)
  • Mechanical changes that don't make a commit (like a rebase) might not have a marker since there's no place to put one.

I oversee all changes directly (I don't use unattended harnesses) and usually hand edit at least a little.

Hi there 👋, I'm Ben

  • 😄 Pronouns: he/him
  • 📫 How to reach me: email or BlueSky @fringetracker.bsky.social

I am an Associate Professor of Statistical Data Science at Macquarie University in Sydney, leading an Astrostatistics Research Group. Before this, I was a Senior Lecturer in Astrophysics and ARC DECRA Fellow at the University of Queensland, a NASA Sagan Fellow at NYU, and I did my DPhil at Balliol College, Oxford.

I research extrasolar planets - planets around other stars - and focus on developing and applying new data science approaches for detecting and characterizing them.

Currently, I'm working on exoplanet direct imaging with JWST's Aperture Masking Interferometer and coronagraphs, interferometry with VLTI, and preparation for the Lazuli Space Observatory. I'm also interested in using radio astronomy to study planets' magnetic interactions with their host stars, and modelling radiocarbon in tree rings as a tracer of ancient solar activity.

Slides for my talks are available here.

some repos

I've contributed to a number of open-source packages for physics, such as

  • virgil, a Jax package for interferometric data analysis
  • dLux, a Jax & equinox library for differentiable, GPU accelerated physical optics
    • docs here!
    • papers at arXiv:2011.09780 and arXiv:2107.00952
    • dLux is a full rewrite of morphine, a physical optics simulation library forked from poppy using Jax for autodiff
  • ticktack, a carbon box modelling library for analysing tree ring radiocarbon data
    • docs here
  • halophot, a pipeline for extracting precise photometry from even very saturated K2 and TESS data
    • papers at arXiv:1708.07462 and arXiv:1908.06981
  • keplersmear, a pipeline for Kepler and K2 using collateral 'smear' data to recover missing lightcurves of bright stars
    • papers at arXiv:1510.00008 and arXiv:1905.09831
  • k2sc, a pipeline for calibrating K2 photometry using Gaussian Processes
    • paper at arXiv:1603.09167
    • docs here
